RESPONDENTS (BY SRI.RAVI V.HOSMANI, AGA FOR R2 TO R5 NOTICE TO R1 IS DISPENSED WITH) THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO i) QUASH THE IMPUGNED SEIZURE MEMO DATED:26.10.2017 BY THE RESPONDENT NO.4 PRODUCED AT ANNEXURE-F TO THE WRIT PETITION. ii) DIRECT THE RESPONDENT NO.4 TO OPEN THE SEAL PUT ON THE PETITIONER'S LOOSE DRINKING WATER UNITS SITUATED AT MUNDRIGI, BALLARI. 3 W.P.No.112161/2017 THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING: ORDER
texts.facts: The petitioner claims that it is running the school named Shree Bhagavan Buddha High School at premises bearing Survey No.112A, Mundragi, Bellary city. The petitioner contends that to cater the needs of the students, of pure drinking water it has installed a water plant in the school premises. 4. Respondent No.4, the Designated Officer/Food Safety Officer issued notice Annexure-E to the petitioner contending that it is running the water plant for the purpose of public consumption without securing the certificate as required under Regulations 2.3.14(17)(18) of the Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales), Regulations, 2011 and licence. Further under Annexure-E the forth respondent has required the petitioner to show cause why the said unit shall not be seized. 5. In pursuance of the said notice, the forth respondent has seized the said unit, under seizer memo Annexure-F dated 26/10/2017.
texts.arguments: The petitioner contends that the unit is seized without providing opportunity of hearing. 6. Sri. Prashant Kadadevar, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that sufficient opportunity to submit reply was not given to the petitioner and seizer of the unit is causing hardship to the students of the school. Thus, the petitioner seeks quashing of Annexure-F. 7. The petitioner contends that the aforesaid provision of Food Safety Act are applicable only to the sale of packaged drinking water and not to the installation seized under Annexure-F as the same is not meant for sale of packaged drinking water. 8. Having issued notice Annexure-E, the 5 t h respondent should have passed an order as to whether the water serving plant in question requires license under Section 31 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that no such order is passed/ communicated to the petitioner.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The petitioner contends that the unit is seized without providing opportunity of hearing. 6. Sri. Prashant Kadadevar, the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that sufficient opportunity to submit reply was not given to the petitioner and seizer of the unit is causing hardship to the students of the school.
texts.respondent_arguments: Thus, the petitioner seeks quashing of Annexure-F. 7. The petitioner contends that the aforesaid provision of Food Safety Act are applicable only to the sale of packaged drinking water and not to the installation seized under Annexure-F as the same is not meant for sale of packaged drinking water. 8. Having issued notice Annexure-E, the 5 t h respondent should have passed an order as to whether the water serving plant in question requires license under Section 31 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. the learned counsel for the petitioner submits that no such order is passed/ communicated to the petitioner.
